drafts.angle: Clay's internal GTM Engineering setup reveals a lesson most teams miss: prioritization and measurement discipline matter more than the tools themselves.

linkedin.content:
Clay uses Clay. That's a given. But what's more interesting is *how* they decide what to build next — and how they know if it worked.

The GTM Engineering Newsletter published a recap of an AMA with Clay's internal GTM Engineer, and the parts worth sitting with aren't the tool stack. They're the operational questions: How do you prioritize use cases when everything feels urgent? What does 'success' actually mean for a GTM system you just shipped?

Most teams sprint to automate something, then move on before they've confirmed it moved a number. Clay's approach — at least as described here — treats scoping and measurement as part of the build, not an afterthought.

If you're running outbound or building GTM infrastructure, that's the habit worth copying before you copy anyone's workflow.

Full recap via The GTM Engineering Newsletter: https://newsletter.gtmengineering.ai/p/gtm-engineering-ama-recap-1-how-clay
